title: Translate the story into an equation
subtitle: Linear equations in two variables · 14 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **14 of the official questions in Linear equations in two variables are this one** — 13 Easy, 1 Medium, 0 Hard.
It is bottom-heavy, which makes it cheap points. Secure it early.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The question ends with 'which equation represents this situation'.
- All four choices are ax + by = c forms using the same numbers in different places.
- The stem gives two per-item values (price, points, speed, rate) and a total.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Pair each per-item value with the variable that counts that item.
- 2) Add the two products and set the sum equal to the total.
- 3) Pick the choice that matches, checking which coefficient sits on which variable.
- For a 'total = part + other part' story, the whole goes alone on one side.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: The wrong choices swap the coefficients between the variables, multiply the total by a rate, or put the rates on the wrong side of the equation.
If you skim for 'the right numbers' you'll pick the swapped version.
For percent-increase stories, you might use the percentages themselves instead of the growth factors (1 + r).

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
The wrong choices swap the coefficients between the variables, multiply the total by a rate, or put the rates on the wrong side of the equation.
If you skim for 'the right numbers' you'll pick the swapped version.
